title: Privacy-preserving SDK telemetry stub playbook
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook describes the pattern, reference implementation, and rollout checklist for a privacy-preserving telemetry stub used by Redwood SDKs during local development and early-stage integration tests. The goal is to let engineers exercise telemetry paths (metrics, events, traces) without sending any customer or production-identifying data to the global telemetry pipeline.

Scope: SDKs and local dev tooling across languages (python/js/go). Does NOT replace production telemetry or privacy controls on customer data in production environments.

Motivation

- Reduce accidental leakage of PII to SaaS telemetry backends during development and demos.
- Provide realistic telemetry semantics locally so developers can test metrics/latency/telemetry-controlled features (feature flags, rollout gating) without requiring backend credentials.
- Offer configurable guarantees: deterministic anonymization for reproducible tests, and randomized differential-privacy-like noise for demo data.

Telemetry goals and constraints

- No raw PII or full user identifiers should leave the developer machine by default.
- Default behavior: local stub retains events locally and exposes a safe summary endpoint.
- Optional forwarding: allow forwarding to a staging telemetry project when "dev-forwarding" is enabled and a developer provides a scoped staging token. Forwarding must mask sensitive fields per mask rules (see Masking rules).
- Observability SLOs for the stub:
  - Local submission latency (in-process): median < 8ms, p95 < 30ms.
  - Local queue flush to disk: < 500ms under normal dev load.
  - Forwarding to staging (when enabled): retry on 5xx up to 3 times with exponential backoff; eventual forwarding success target 98% for accepted events.

Design summary

1) Local-first stub process: SDKs use a local HTTP socket (default: 127.0.0.1:43211) or in-process API to submit telemetry. The stub supports three modes via configuration: "off", "local-only", "local+forward".
2) Field-level privacy adapters: configurable mask/transform rules applied before any network egress. Rules include: hash(id), truncate(email), drop(phone), redact-paths(jsonpath).
3) Sampling and noise: per-event sampling (default 5% for high-volume events) and optional Laplace/Gaussian noise injection for numeric metrics in demo mode.
4) Test harness compatibility: the stub can run in-memory for unit tests, or as a standalone binary for local integration. It includes a deterministic replay file format for golden tests.

Masking rules (default set)

| Field matcher | Default action | Notes |
|---------------|----------------|-------|
| $.user.id | hash(SHA256, salt=dev-salt) | deterministic; same id => same hash for local debugging |
| $.user.email | truncate(3) + hash(domain) | preserves domain shape but not full address |
| $.session.token | drop | never forwarded |
| $.request.headers.authorization | drop | never forwarded |
| $.customer.* | redact | top-level customer object redacted unless allowlist enabled |

Configuration reference (yaml)

```
stub:
  mode: "local-only" # off | local-only | local+forward
  listen: "127.0.0.1:43211"
  allowlist_forward_fields: ["metric.name","feature.flag"]
  masking:
    salt: "dev-salt"
    rules:
      - path: "$.user.id"
        action: "hash"
      - path: "$.user.email"
        action: "truncate_and_hash"
  sampling:
    default_rate: 0.05
  forward:
    staging_token: null
    endpoint: "https://telemetry-staging.internal.redwood/v1/events"
    retry:
      count: 3
      base_delay_ms: 200
```

SDK integration patterns

- Initialization: SDKs should detect a local stub via environment variable REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_STUB=1 or via the standard config file (~/.redwood/sdk_telemetry.yaml). If detected, the SDK routes telemetry traffic to the stub automatically.
- Fallback: If stub is not reachable, SDK should fall back to in-memory sink and emit a single console warning once per process.
- Consent/opt-in: Developers must explicitly enable forwarding with REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_FORWARD=1 and provide REDWOOD_STAGING_TOKEN.

Local quickstart (python example)

1) Install the stub (dev package):
```
pip install redwood-telemetry-stub==0.3.0.dev
```
2) Start the stub (standalone):
```
redwood-telemetry-stub start --config ~/.redwood/stub-config.yaml
```
3) Point SDK to stub via env:
```
export REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_STUB=1
export REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_ADDR=127.0.0.1:43211
```
4) Run the app and exercise telemetry paths. Verify local dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:43212/ui 

SDK snippet (python)

```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="local-dev", telemetry_enabled=True)
client.track_event("search.performed", {"user": {"id": "alice@example.com", "email": "alice@example.com"}})
```

Telemetry stub CLI reference (selected)

- redwood-telemetry-stub start --config <path> --foreground
- redwood-telemetry-stub status
- redwood-telemetry-stub replay <replay-file> --verify
- redwood-telemetry-stub export-snapshot ./snapshot.json

Privacy patterns and guidance

- Default safe mode: shipping SDKs must default to "local-only" mode with a strict mask set. No opt-out should downgrade masking.
- Developer override: allowlist-based unmasking limited to machine-local config and requires explicit flag. Do NOT store unmasking flags in source control.
- Differential privacy guidance: only enable noise addition for non-security-critical demo metrics. Document the seed and parameters used in the test harness for reproducibility.
- Golden tests: store only the anonymized/replayed outputs. Add a presubmit check to prevent checked-in replay files that contain unhashed PII.

Examples: anonymization vs hashing

- Anonymization (recommended for demos): replace email with "user-<N>@example.invalid" where N is stable-per-run.
- Hashing (recommended for local debug): SHA256(id + dev-salt) retains ability to correlate events across sessions without exposing original id.

Operational runbook for SDK teams

1) Smoke test: after merging SDK change, run unit tests with stub-in-memory and full integration tests against the stub binary.
2) Canaries: when enabling forward mode for a team, start with a single developer or CI job with REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_FORWARD enabled and monitor staging project for anomalies for 48 hours.
3) Incident steps if staging receives PII:
   1. Immediately disable forwarding tokens (rotate staging_token).
   2. Run `redwood-telemetry-stub export-snapshot` on affected dev boxes (if possible) and collect for triage.
   3. Notify Security + Privacy teams and follow incident_response_security runbook.

Rollout checklist

- [ ] DX SDK: add stub autodetection and env var logic (owner: SDK team).
- [ ] Telemetry Service: publish mask rule schema and validator (owner: telemetry-service).
- [ ] CI: add tests that ensure no raw email patterns appear in replay outputs (owner: DX infra).
- [ ] Docs: add a short tutorial to dev onboarding and sample repository (owner: developer-experience).
- [ ] Security review: confirm compliance with privacy policy and record evidence (owner: security).

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: SDK Developer Experience (engineering).
- Supporting owner: telemetry-service (engineering).
- Security reviewer: Data Protection Office (security).
- On-call for stub: dx-shared-oncall (pager duty alias).

Appendix A — Example sanitization implementation (JS)

```
function sanitizePayload(payload, rules) {
  // simple example: hash user.id, redact customer
  if (payload.user && payload.user.id) {
    payload.user.id = sha256(payload.user.id + rules.salt).slice(0, 16)
  }
  if (payload.customer) {
    payload.customer = "<redacted>"
  }
  return payload
}
```

Appendix B — Replay file format (JSON-lines)

- Each line: {"ts":"ISO8601","event":"<name>","payload":{...},"sanitized":true}
- Use `redwood-telemetry-stub replay file.ndjson --verify` to assert all lines are sanitized.

Notes and rationale

This playbook prefers conservative defaults to reduce accidental data leaks while still providing high-fidelity developer feedback. It is intentionally language-agnostic: SDK owners should implement the stub client idiomatically for their language but conform to the same masking schema and CLI behavior so that cross-team tests remain stable.

If questions or edge cases arise, ping the SDK DX channel (#dx-sdk) and create a short issue linking the failing example and the replay snapshot.
